Measured figure/ground: glyph patch (378,215,14×14) = rgb(195,150,74) vs surrounding disc (340,270,20×16) = rgb(153,103,8) → relative luminance 0.338 vs 0.167, a contrast ratio of about 1.8:1. The reference's emblem/field separation is several times that. The over-lightening is the combined effect of the screen's mix-blend-mode:color layer plus the interior screen layer the implementer added on top of TeamCrest's already-lightened gold well; REFERENCE-SPEC calls for 'a dark team-tinted interior' with the glyph luminous against it.
findings.fix: Do the gold grade at source in src/components/TeamCrest.tsx: in the `gold` branch keep the interior well DARK (the reference's field is dark, not #92693B all over — that sample is the lit rim), fill EMBLEMS[teamId] with var(--color-key) and #FFF4D0 for the top facet with a --color-key drop-shadow, and add the bright inner glow ring. Then remove the compensating mix-blend-mode:color layer and soften the interior screen layer in KeyCeremony.tsx so the well is not lifted twice.

findings.what: The handle posts carry two hard hairline stripes down the shaft with blunt square ends at different vertical extents, and the shaft is the same width as the end pads instead of the reference's narrow shaft between wider lugs.
findings.evidence: Post crop at 5× in both. BUILD: a near-black 2px stripe runs down the shaft at x≈137 from y≈600 to y≈770 and a cream stripe at x≈145 from y≈578 to y≈796 — different lengths, both terminating in flat square ends mid-form where they meet the end pads, so each stripe reads as a pasted line rather than a cylinder edge. The silhouette is one uniform capsule with a screw at each end. REFERENCE: the post is a narrow cylindrical bar (about 55% of the pad width) joined to two rounded-square lugs by a visible shouldered transition, shaded by one broad soft gradient with no hairlines, mottled with aged patina and rust flecks; there is no stripe to stub out. The build's posts also carry no patina at all, against CLAUDE.md's 'rust patina in crevices and along lower edges'.
findings.fix: In KeyCeremony.tsx lines 631–669: narrow the shaft rect to ~0.55 × padR*2 and keep the pads at their current radius so a real shoulder appears; replace the two stripe rects with a single horizontal linearGradient across the shaft (dark → highlight at ~30% → dark) so there are no line ends to stub; add a low-opacity patina/noise overlay along the lower third.

findings.what: The key rail is markedly paler and flatter than the reference's aged brass bar, its rivets are flat dots rather than domed heads, and the keys are geometric primitives.
findings.evidence: Sampled the rail face between the left screw and the first key. BUILD (300,1408,60×24) = rgb(173,135,88) #ad8758. REFERENCE (300,1600,80×30) = rgb(118,82,42) #76522a — the build's rail is ~1.5× brighter and yellower, which makes it the brightest large object in the lower third of the frame, whereas in the reference the hot key is. The reference bar also carries a crisp lit top chamfer, rust patina streaks and domed brass rivets; the build has a plain vertical gradient and two 4px flat dots. The keys themselves: reference has an ornate pierced bow, a collared shank and a toothed bit; the build has a plain circle, a straight bar and three small rectangles.
findings.fix: Deepen the rail gradient toward #76522a (leave the top ~6% clear so the chamfer specular survives), add patina streaks along its lower edge, and give the rivets a radial gradient with a top-left glint. Give the key glyph a pierced bow and a two-tooth bit so it reads as an antique key rather than an icon.

findings.what: The hot key's rising smoke plume does not appear in any capture.
findings.evidence: Took three independent screenshots (refute3-key.png, k2.png, k3.png), each ~350ms after networkidle with animations live. In all three the region above the hot key's bow (x 440–640, y 1220–1440) shows only the key's own bloom and two small amber spark dashes — no smoke of any kind. The reference has a prominent plume rising roughly 2.5 key-heights past the bow and up over the 'KEY 02' line, and it is one of the two things that mark the new key as newly forged. The implementer's rewrite deliberately caps the puffs at --rise of −16/−21/−26px and ramps opacity 0 → 0.5 → 0.22 → 0, which is both far shorter than the reference and easy to catch at zero.
findings.fix: Lengthen the puff travel to roughly 2–2.5 key-heights and stagger the three delays so at least one puff is above 0.3 opacity at any moment, so the plume is continuously present rather than intermittently absent.

findings.what: Plate and brass faces are ~40 L brighter and less saturated than the reference — the whole board reads pale sand/khaki where the reference reads bronze. (The implementer's rejection is SOUND: the gradients live in shared theme.css, not Board.tsx. But the defect is still on screen, so it is filed here.)
findings.evidence: Sampled the same features in both images (5x5 mean). Row-plate face beside the rank chip: build #998168 rgb(153,129,104) L=132 vs reference #715945 rgb(113,89,69) L=93. Header inner panel: build #9f8354 L=134 vs reference #705c4a L=95. Day-rail bar: build #9c8052 L=131 vs reference #6b5442 L=88. The bottom stop already agrees (build #5f4a36 L=77 vs ref L=75), so it is the top of the gradient that is wrong, not the whole ramp. Build's plate-hi sample (153,129,104) is outside REFERENCE-SPEC's definition-of-done band #6A5240–#98795E. Side-by-side header crops at 3-4x confirm it by eye: reference is a bronze plate with a gold engraved line, ours is a sandy tan band.
findings.fix: In src/theme.css drop the top three stops of `.plate`/`.steel`/`.steel-raised` ~35 L and the top two stops of `.brass-band` ~35 L, shifting them ~8 deg toward red; leave `--color-plate-lo` alone. Target: plate face L 90-95, header/rail brass L 88-95.

findings.what: Rust reads as bright orange blotching painted across lit plate faces, not as oxidation in crevices and along lower edges. It is the loudest AI-tell left on the screen and it is a regression from the previous pass (rust census went 0.17% -> 1.66% vs the reference's 1.03%).
findings.evidence: Footer strip, build: rust patch #74583e L=93 against the clean strip beside it #4c3a27 L=61 — the rust is 32 L BRIGHTER than the metal, high-contrast mottle covering the right ~55% of the plate face. Reference footer: rust #5f4836 L=77 against clean #6a503f L=86 — 9 L DARKER than the metal, a soft stain confined to the far-right end and the bottom edge. Same problem on the header: my 4x crop shows hard-edged orange islands across the lower half of the header's lit face; the reference header's face is clean bronze with no visible patina at all.
findings.fix: In Board.tsx's `Oxide`, make the pigment darken rather than lighten (target -10 to -18 L against the host surface, same hue), cut the alpha/coverage roughly in half, soften the mask edges, and restrict placement to the plate's lower lip, the shadow side and bolt seats. Remove it from the header's lit face entirely.

findings.what: Team crest interiors are far darker and more violet than the reference's mid-tone team-tinted disc, so eight medallions read as black portholes with a neon decal instead of lit enamel.
findings.evidence: WARRIORS crest, sampling the interior field between the glyph arms: build #4a1c35 L=45 (top), #301321 L=29 (left), #3e172d L=37 (right). Reference at the equivalent positions reads a warm maroon/mauve — the clean interior samples land L=53-75 and the 6x crop shows an evenly lit mid-tone disc filling the bezel. The build's 8x crop shows a near-black radial with the pink bloom only immediately around the glyph.
findings.fix: In src/components/TeamCrest.tsx lift the interior fill to roughly `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-team-<token>) 26%, #2a2018)` (L 60-80), keep the top-left key light on the disc, and keep the glyph luminous.

findings.what: Day-rail sockets are flat black bores in a thin brass ring — the one place on the board that still reads as holes punched in a strip rather than machined hardware.
findings.evidence: 5x crops of both rails: the reference socket is a heavy brass housing with four dark notch slots at N/E/S/W, a wide bevelled collar lit from the top left, and a recessed BRONZE face inside — future days are dim bronze faces, still metal, and the lit socket's teal fills the face and ignites its four notches. The build draws a thin flat brass annulus around a pure black bore (~#1a1410) with no notches, no bevel and no collar; the three future days read as punched holes, and the current day is a teal sphere sitting on top of the rail whose halo does not touch the housing.
findings.fix: In src/components/DayRail.tsx (SocketRail) add four dark notch slots at N/E/S/W to the socket housing, thicken the collar with a top-left specular, and give unlit sockets a bronze face, e.g. `radial-gradient(circle at 40% 34%, #3a2c20 0%, #241a12 62%, #140d08 100%)` instead of `--color-well`. Seat the lit face flush in the collar and let its teal spill onto the notches and the rail.

findings.what: The golden keys are hairline wire outlines that hang out of the bottom of their recess — the most important object in the app is the weakest-drawn thing in the row.
findings.evidence: 5x crop of the key rail: build keys are ~1.5px-stroke outlines (a thin circle bow, a hairline stem, two tiny teeth); the bows sit above the slot's top lip AND the bits hang roughly 40% of the key's height BELOW the slot's bottom lip, so they read as brass hooks laid over the plate rather than keys hanging in a recess, and the lit key's emission is a faint local wash. The reference's keys are solid modelled gold — thick bow ring, collared shaft, chunky bit — sitting inside the slot with only the bow overhanging the top lip, and the lit ones bloom visibly onto the capsule floor.
findings.fix: In the KeyGlyph/key-rail code thicken the key to a filled solid form (bow ring ~2.5px stroke, shaft ~3px, real bit), scale it so the bit ends at the slot's lower lip with only the bow overhanging the top, and give the lit key a tight warm bloom onto the capsule floor. Keep the dark silhouette for empty capacity.

findings.what: The header's 'double brass frame' is two dark hairlines on a flat face, and its corners are square where the reference's are chamfered.
findings.evidence: 4x crops: the reference header has an outer dark bevel, then a bright GOLD engraved line, then a dark channel, then the brushed interior, with a 45-degree cut corner on both the frame and the inner panel. The build draws two thin dark lines only — no lit engraving, no channel, no chamfer — so the frame reads as printed on the surface rather than machined into it.
findings.fix: In Board.tsx's header composition, paint the inner frame as a 1px `--color-brass-hi` engraved line with a 1px dark channel above it (lit top-left, `--color-brass-lo` bottom-right), and chamfer the header's outer and inner corners ~8px.

findings.what: Corner fasteners are still 2-3x the visual mass of the reference's row rivets, because the washer seat does not scale with the head.
findings.evidence: Build (5x crop): brass slotted head ~6 CSS sitting in a dark washer seat that reads ~9 CSS across, at all four corners of every row plate, the header and the footer. Reference (3.6x crop): row fasteners are plain brass domes ~3 CSS with no dark seat ring and no slot; they are quiet marks, not dark squares.
findings.fix: Scale `.screw`'s washer rings off the head size in src/theme.css (`0 0 0 calc(var(--sw,11px)*0.14) ...`, `*0.23`, `*0.41`) so a 6px head gets a ~2.5px seat, then drop the row screws to ~4px and the slot at that size.

findings.what: Crest glyphs are 2-3 stroke geometric marks covering ~60% of the interior; WARRIORS in particular is a plain X that reads as a placeholder.
findings.evidence: 8x crops: the reference emblem is detailed line art (gear + piston + two small gears) filling ~85% of the interior with internal cut-outs and an engraved edge. The build's WARRIORS glyph is two crossed bars with a small diamond; PEARLS is a generic figure, INNOCENT a plain heart, GEMS a diamond-in-diamond. At row scale they read flatter and less specific than the taste target.
findings.fix: In src/components/TeamCrest.tsx give each team a 2-3 element emblem (silhouette + one internal detail), scale the glyph to ~80-85% of the interior diameter, and add a 1px darker inner edge so it reads engraved-and-lit rather than pasted on.

findings.what: The commit discharge never blows out. The tube's hottest pixel is a neutral grey, not white-hot — so the single most important beat on the screen reads as a soft blurred lamp rather than an arc erupting.
findings.evidence: I captured the released/seated commit frame myself (scratchpad/sk3/x-seated.png, plus t=80/250/450ms frames). Max-luminance scan over the whole tube region (x130-650, y1370-1450): max L=223, #dfdfde, PURE-WHITE PIXEL COUNT = 0. Same scan on reference 03 (x330-760, y1500-1620): max L=255, #ffffff, pure-white pixel count = 4885. Sampling the core directly at (375,1400) gives #dddcdb at t=80ms and t=200ms — never white. The implementer's rejection says 'On a released frame (scratchpad/shots/r3-c-seated.png) the core was already pure #ffffff'; I ran the same max scan on THEIR OWN r3-c-seated.png and it returns max L=223 #dfdfde, 0 pure-white pixels. The rejection is contradicted by the artifact it cites. Whole-frame spec% is 2.73 vs reference 03's 4.4, consistent with the missing blowout. Note pure white IS reachable elsewhere in the build — the pull-adds socket measures #fffdf9 L253 — so this is specific to the tube core.
findings.fix: Take the blown core sprite to a true #FFFFFF at full opacity at the seat peak (CLAUDE.md --accent-hot is #FFFFFF). Something upstream is capping it around 0.87 — most likely the sprite's own opacity or a blend under the teal bloom. Verify by re-running a max-L scan on the released frame until pure-white pixels appear at the core.

findings.what: The discharge lights the row plates above but not the lever housing the emitter is bolted to. The nearest surface to the light source stays brown while the far ones go cool — physically backwards.
findings.evidence: Sampled the same housing-interior points in my rest shot and my seated shot. Upper interior beside the rails (250,1300): rest #4a3720 L57 -> commit #3e3627 L55 — unchanged and still warm brown (R-B = +23). Lower interior (387,1500): rest #463522 L55 -> commit #405040 L75, warmth 0. Reference at the equivalent points: upper (380,1400) #36251b L40 -> #4c6859 L97; lower (536,1680) #423022 L51 -> #4c8a7d L124 — the entire housing plate turns teal-green, +57 to +73 L. Meanwhile the build's row plates DO respond (row 7 face (320,986) #65533f L85 -> #706350 L100), so the wall wash the implementer added works upward and skips its own plate. Visible in the crops: reference 03's housing interior is bathed teal edge to edge; the build's stays chocolate brown outside a local bloom around the tube.
findings.fix: Extend the discharge wash to the lever housing plate itself, at the highest intensity of anything on screen (it is closest to the emitter), with falloff outward from the tube. Same layer that lights the rows, just not clipped to exclude the housing.

findings.what: The emitter tube is not glass. Its bore is a uniformly saturated teal slab with a fat neutral-grey stripe, and it is about 1.6x longer than the reference's, so it spans almost rail to rail instead of sitting as a short cylinder mid-track.
findings.evidence: Vertical scan through the build's tube at x=375 (rest): #517c71 L114, #2fa59d L139, #cecdcb L205 (core), #32a79e L141, then #1a1a14 L26 below — a saturated teal band over a black bore. Horizontal scan at y=1409 across the whole tube: every interior sample has B far above R (#366b63 R54/B99, #2da29a R45/B154). Reference 02 vertical scan at x=536: #4d4b3e, #4f5144, #3d4641, #3a453f — the bore is a desaturated grey-green GLASS (R and B within ~15 of each other) at L50-80, with a single thin filament sample #77b0a9 L163. Extent: build teal band runs x158-625 = 233 CSS px = 60% of the 390 screen; reference glass runs roughly x336-744 of 1080 = 147 CSS = 38%. In the crops (sk3/c-rail.png vs sk3/r-rail.png) the reference shows glass wall, a dark bore and metal electrode rods entering from the collars; the build shows a rounded-rect capsule filled edge to edge with teal.
findings.fix: Make the bore read as glass: near-neutral dark interior with a top specular streak along the cylinder, visible wall thickness, and electrode rods from each collar. Confine the teal to the filament plus its bloom rather than filling the bore. Shorten the tube to roughly 145-150 CSS so there is a real gap between the collars and the rails for the commit branches to jump.

findings.what: For ~400ms after release, a committed row renders one MORE lit socket than its true check-in count — the leader watches the discharge and reads 0.6 where the state is 0.5.
findings.evidence: Same session, three captures. Selected frame: Innocent shows 4 amber sockets + exactly one white-hot at socket 5 (x508-536 reads #fffdf9 L253), sockets 6-7 dark. Data confirms one event lands (punctuality events 119 -> 121 total for 2 teams; aria-label goes 'Innocent, 4 of 7' -> 'Innocent, 5 of 7'). But the seated render at t=80/250ms samples socket 6 (x=560) at #e4cc76 L203 — lit — while socket 7 stays dark L29. At t=450ms socket 6 drops to #20160f L24 and the row settles at the correct 5. Rust Revival Co. behaves identically: 3 lit at rest, one white preview at socket 4, 5 lit sockets rendered during the discharge, 4 at settle. Reference 03 shows no such over-count: the already-earned sockets keep team colour and only the pull's own sockets are white.
findings.fix: During the seat/afterglow the landing socket is being drawn on top of the already-incremented tick count. Drive the flash off the pre-commit tick index (or clear the preview the moment the event is appended) so the lit count never exceeds PUNCTUALITY ticks at any frame.

findings.what: The cog knob's toothed ring reads as a black sawtooth halo rather than a brass gear, and its dark inner dish is far too small — so the part reads as a tan disc ringed in black instead of the reference's bright brass ring around a dark well.
findings.evidence: Ring scan of the tooth annulus. Build (centre 679,475, r=34): top-left arc mean L107, bottom-right arc mean L46, and the tooth valleys bottom out at #0e0906 L10 at BOTH diagonals — (656,452) #0e0906 and (702,498) #0e0906. Reference (centre 929,807, r=42): top-left mean L125, bottom-right mean L71, with samples like (900,778) #c0a27c L166 and (960,838) #776245 L100 — brass on the shadow side too. So the build's shadow-side ring is 25 L darker than the reference's and its valleys are pure black. Proportion: in sk3/c-knob.png the dark inner recess is ~32 of 73 device px = 44% of the knob diameter; in sk3/r-knob.png it is ~54 of 88 = 61%. Side by side the reference reads 'bright brass ring around a dark dish with a bright star'; the build reads 'tan disc with a small hole, wearing a black gear'.
findings.fix: Give the teeth brass bodies with dark valleys rather than black bodies — the valley floor should sit around --brass-lo, not near black — and keep the annulus above L70 on the shadow side. Open the inner recess to ~60% of the knob diameter so the bright torus reads as a ring.

findings.what: The lever footing's nameplate polarity is inverted and the casting is visibly seamed, so it reads as two feet with a slot between them rather than one brass casting.
findings.evidence: sk3/r-foot.png: the reference footing is one continuous bright brass casting with a RAISED plaque (notched corners, a rivet at each end) sitting on top of it, brighter than the surrounding brass, with dark engraved letters. sk3/c-foot.png: the build has a left pad and a right pad with a long RECESSED trough between them whose face is darker than the pads, the caption engraved into the trough, and a dark vertical seam visible where each pad meets the trough. Overall height is right (both ~28-30 CSS), so it is the polarity and the seams, not the mass.
findings.fix: Raise the nameplate as a plaque above a continuous brass web (brighter than its surround, dark letters) and close the two seams so the pads and the web read as one casting.

findings.what: The `ALL` tab is a 32x15 tap target — less than half the height of the header controls that were just enlarged for exactly this reason.
findings.evidence: DOM measurement of every focusable on the route: 'Back to board 42x24', 'Previous activity 22x24', 'Next activity 22x24', team rows '364x56', 'Commit lever 364x26' — and 'ALL 32x15'. It is the only control on the screen under 24px tall, and it is the one that arms the whole stack. (Everything else in the audit is clean: scrollWidth 390, no overflow, no truncation, all eight rows 364x56 on a 64px pitch, fonts are Oswald / Barlow Condensed / JetBrains Mono only, no × anywhere, rows are real buttons with aria-pressed and are keyboard operable.)
findings.fix: Raise the ALL tab to at least 24px tall to match the header rockers, keeping it on the housing's brass top margin.

findings.what: The team seal is still a glowing orange vent-disc, not a brass coin carrying a raised emblem — and its brass ring is lit on the left only.
findings.evidence: Horizontal row scan through the seal's vertical centre. BUILD (refute3-teamsheet.png, y=160 device, x 242→540): left ring L=126,72,153 then a sustained interior plateau of L=189 with R-B=148 (flat pale orange) across ~130px, then the right side collapses to L=30,72,62,67,66,41 with R-B 34–55 — i.e. the right half of the ring is at wall/plate luminance while the left half is bright brass. REFERENCE (05-team-sheet.jpg, y=215, x 345→725): left ring L=122–148, right ring L=137–156, both R-B 79–93; the interior alternates brass L≈99–106 with rust-orange emblem L≈49–93 (R-B 117–137). Zoomed crop confirms: build interior is 12 pale rounded-rectangle teeth on a flat orange bloom (max rgb 248,235,204, L=235 — brighter than the total numeral's L=228), reading as a fan or vent lamp with no visible emitter; the reference interior is a rust-orange gear + flame + wrench silhouette raised on radial-brushed brass, and the brightest thing on the reference screen is the total numeral (L=247) not the coin (L=239). The implementer listed this in shared_needs, i.e. never attempted it.
findings.fix: In TeamCrest.tsx, when `label` is set, fill the coin interior with radial-brushed brass in the --brass-hi/--brass band (reference ring specular rgb 236,212,160, body rgb 196,165,109), symmetric left-to-right with the falloff running top-left to bottom-right, not left to right. Delete the full-disc orange bloom. Draw the emblem as a layered silhouette on top of the brass — gear ring behind, flame/wrench in front — in the team colour with a gold specular edge and only a tight local bloom.

findings.what: The seal's circular legend covers only ~150° of the coin, and a bezel screw sits directly on the leading letters of RUST REVIVAL CO.
findings.evidence: DOM: the legend <textPath> bounding box is x 157.3→232.9, y 18.4→40.6 — 75.6 CSS px wide inside a 148px seal, so the arc spans roughly the top third. At 3.2x zoom the arc runs from about 10 o'clock to 2 o'clock and terminates at 'CO.'; a dark bezel-screw dot lands on the 'R'/'U' of RUST and a pale one immediately after 'CO.'. The arc also crosses the header frame's pale brass rail, so 'REVIVAL' loses contrast against it. In the reference the legend wraps ~250° (roughly 8 o'clock round to 4 o'clock), is engraved dark into a bright gold ring band, is fully contained on the coin's own material, and no bezel screw falls under it. Also flagged by the implementer in shared_needs and not attempted.
findings.fix: In TeamCrest.tsx, extend the legend textPath to ~250° with a matching type size, raise the ring luminance under the arc to L≈170–210 so the type reads as engraving on gold, and relocate the bezel screws to 0/90/180/270° (or out beyond the legend radius) so none intersects the arc.

findings.what: The OFF toggle is bright cool-grey silver hardware with an unmotivated bright rim, where the reference's unpowered toggle is the darkest, warmest thing in its row.
findings.evidence: Cleanliness row, sampled in both. BUILD: OFF knob rgb 192,183,165 (L=184, R-B=27) with a vertically brushed neutral face; OFF track specular band rgb 171,160,142 (L=161, R-B=29) and track body rgb 135,124,106 (L=125). The surrounding plate is rgb ~123,90,64 (L≈97, R-B≈58), so the unpowered control is 60–90 L brighter than the warm plate and ~30 points lower in R-B — it reads silver against brown, and the bright cream/gold hairline around the capsule's lower-right is a glow with no emitter on a control that is switched off. REFERENCE (Lesson Knowledge row): OFF knob rgb 76,57,43 (L=61, R-B=33), track rgb 45–49,28–32,20–22 (L=32–36) against a plate at L≈85 — the unpowered toggle is darker than its plate and carries no bright rim. REFERENCE-SPEC tokens agree: --off-track #614A39 (L≈62), --off-knob #543E2E (L≈53).
findings.fix: In Breaker.tsx, drive the OFF state from --off-track/--off-knob rather than a light neutral: sink the track to L≈35 warm brown, make the knob a dark warm brass cylinder at L≈60 with only a thin top-left specular, and remove the bright lower-right rim band entirely from the unpowered state (keep it only for ON, where an emitter exists).

findings.what: A hung golden key throws almost no light onto the wall — the key is the most important object in the app and here it lights nothing.
findings.evidence: Shot /#/team/knights (day 1, 1 key) at 390x844 dpr2. BUILD row scan at the key shaft (y=1600, x 60→200): peak L=144 on the shaft, and the wall immediately beside it reads L=35, 23, 16, 12, 12, 12 — back to bare-wall level (L≈12) within ~30 device px. REFERENCE row scan at the key shafts (y=1850, x 80→300): shaft peaks L=202 and 183, and the wall around them is lifted to L=56–96 across roughly 120 ref px on each side, versus L=32 at the far left of the same row. So the reference key pools warm gold light onto the wall over ~43 CSS px; the build's decays to nothing in ~15. Key geometry itself now matches (bow ≈21 CSS wide, length ≈57 CSS vs reference 20.6 / 61) and the disc banding the implementer fixed is gone.
findings.fix: In KeyRail.tsx, widen the hung-key bloom radius roughly 3x and raise its floor so the wall beside a lit key sits around L 55–90 rather than L 12, keeping the same smooth multi-stop radial (a wide low-alpha wash under the existing tight core), and lift the key body itself from peak L≈144 to ≈200.

findings.what: The Good Deed and Behavior glyphs still do not read as a handshake and a caped figure — the claimed redraw did not land.
findings.evidence: Side-by-side crops of the glyph column at matched scale. GOOD DEED — reference: a solid, filled, embossed brass handshake, two hands clasping horizontally, unmistakable. Build: two thin single-stroke forearms angling down from the upper-left and upper-right into a small lump at the bottom-centre; it reads as a slingshot or two pipes joining, and the 'fingers' are three short stubs that do not wrap anything. BEHAVIOR — reference: a solid filled symmetric hero, filled disc head merged into the shoulders, arms akimbo with closed triangles, cape flaring right. Build: a thin stick figure with an open donut head, asymmetric limbs, splayed legs and an open outline arc on the right that reads as a wing or shield, not a cape. Both reference glyphs are solid filled silhouettes; both build glyphs are thin outline strokes, so the weight is wrong as well as the shape. (Lesson Knowledge is improved but its outline is a lumpy blob rather than the reference's clean brain silhouette.)
findings.fix: In TeamSheet.tsx redraw both as filled silhouettes rather than stroked line art, matching the reference's solid embossed treatment: Good Deed as two overlapping filled hands clasped on a horizontal axis; Behavior as a filled symmetric figure with the head merged into the shoulders, closed akimbo triangles and a filled cape.

findings.what: The punctuality readout `3 / 7 · 0.3` is orphaned — it sits closer to the Memory Verse plate than to the plate it belongs to.
findings.evidence: DOM: punctuality plate y 349→417; readout y 430→439; Memory Verse plate y 439→507. findings.what: The `+ KEY` tab is dark type struck into brass and has no diagonal chamfer break; the reference reads it as bright cream on a chamfer-separated tab.
findings.evidence: Build crop of the key rail: `+ KEY` is rendered as a dark brown face (DOM shows two stacked Oswald 20px `+ KEY` texts at y 752.5 and 753.4 — the struck/emboss pair), separated from the bar by a plain vertical seam with a slightly lighter rectangle behind it. Reference crop: `+ KEY` is bright cream on brass, and the tab is separated by a diagonal chamfer notch cut through the bar with rust patina bleeding across the joint. The disabled gate itself is legitimate (`disabled={locked || !directorMode}`), but the default delivered state is what the screen shows.
findings.fix: In KeyRail.tsx keep the gate but bring the gated legend up in luminance so it still reads as the reference's tab (cream at reduced weight rather than dark-on-brass), and cut the tab away from the bar with the reference's diagonal chamfer notch instead of a straight seam.

findings.what: The header brass frame has no rust patina and its inner corner is rounded rather than mitred.
findings.evidence: Lower-left corner crops at matched zoom. Reference: a wide brass band with a 45° mitred inner corner, an engraved hairline running parallel inside the band, a slotted screw, and clear orange rust speckle along the frame's inner edge and lower run plus vertical rust streaks down the left jamb. Build: a narrower flat brass band with a rounded inner corner, a slotted screw, and zero rust — no orange speckle anywhere on the frame. REFERENCE-SPEC §Screen 05 calls for 'Rust patina along the frame's lower corners' and 'outer bevel + engraved inner line'.
findings.fix: In TeamSheet.tsx apply the existing rust-creep treatment to the header frame's lower corners and lower run, and mitre the frame's inner corner at 45° to match the plate rows' chamfer language.

findings.what: The day tabs are 20px tall on a 37px pitch — off the 8px grid and well under the tap-target minimum.
findings.evidence: DOM on /#/team/rustco: five buttons at 30x20, lefts 106/143/180/217/254 (37px pitch, 7px gaps), 'ARR' set in Oswald 10px. Neither 20 nor 37 nor 7 is on the 8px grid, and 20px tall is less than half the 44px minimum. Measuring the reference tabs gives ≈31x21 CSS on a ≈39px pitch, so the geometry does match the concept render — this is a CLAUDE.md grid and reachability violation rather than a mismatch, and the implementer correctly identified it as DayRail's, not the screen's.
findings.fix: In DayRail.tsx (variant='tabs') move to a 32px tab on a 40px pitch (8px gaps) and give each button a >=44px invisible hit area, keeping the visible octagon at roughly the reference's proportions.
